title: I Played Hardcore Minecraft for 100 Days in a Single Biome
creator: Kenji Arai
description:
100 days of hardcore Minecraft, but I can never leave the mushroom island. No villages, no trees, no mobs. How long can I last?

Become a channel member: click Join under the video for early access, member-only streams and a shoutout in the credits.

Seed is in the pinned comment.

sentences.t: Day one, and I've just spawned on a mushroom island in the middle of the ocean.
The rule for this challenge is simple, I can never leave this island, not even for a second.
And it's hardcore, so if I die, the video's over.
Mushroom islands are honestly one of the weirdest places in the game.
There are no trees, no normal animals, and hostile mobs can't spawn here at all.
So in theory it's safe, but in practice I have no wood, which is a massive problem.
Days two to five, I'm trying to figure out how to get wood without trees.
And the answer is giant mushrooms.
If I grow mushrooms on mycelium with some bone meal, they turn into huge mushrooms, and I can break those for stems.
I'm getting bone meal from, let's see, nothing, because there are no skeletons.
So I'm farming bone meal from a composter, stuffing it full of mushrooms.
Day eight, my first crafting table.
I nearly cried.
Seriously, eight days for a crafting table is a personal worst.
Quick shoutout while I'm building, to everyone who's become a member of the channel.
If you hit the join button under the video, you get every episode a day early, plus member-only streams where we play hardcore together.
And members get their names in the credits at the end of every video, so this week you'll see about fifty names scroll past.
You guys are the reason I can keep doing hundred-day videos, because these take weeks to record.
Day fifteen.
The cows on this island are mooshrooms, which are red cows with mushrooms growing out of them.
If I milk one with a bowl, I get mushroom stew, which is basically infinite free food.
So food is officially solved.
Days twenty to forty, I'm building a base into the side of the island's biggest hill.
I'm digging down because stone gives me tools, and I've finally got a stone pickaxe and a stone sword.
At day thirty-two I hit iron, which is a huge deal, because iron means a bucket, and a bucket means water and farming.
Day forty-seven, the closest I came to dying.
I was digging down too fast, broke into a cave, and there were mobs in it, because caves don't count as the mushroom biome.
A creeper came round the corner and blew up right next to me.
I had two hearts left.
Two hearts.
I sealed myself in with dirt and just ate stew for about five minutes with my heart going crazy.
Days fifty to eighty, I've gone fishing crazy.
Fishing is the only way I can get stuff like enchanted books and name tags on this island.
And on day seventy-three, I fished up a bow with power three, which is ridiculous luck.
Days eighty to a hundred.
I built a lighthouse on the edge of the island, a mooshroom farm, and a huge mushroom garden on the roof of my base.
And on day one hundred, I'm still alive, on the island, with full diamond armor that I mined out of the caves underneath.
So yeah, the mushroom island turned out to be a pretty good home after all.
Let me know which biome I should try next, and I'll see you in the next hundred days.
